title: 石破氏ら戒告の自民 引き締め躍起
body:
自民党執行部が９日、消費税減税・支援金法案の採決前に退席した石破茂前首相ら４人の戒告処分を早々に決めたのは、１１日の参院での審議入りを前に、党内の引き締めを図る狙いからだ。総裁経験者も初の処分対象とし、少数与党で臨む参院の採決で退席や欠席の動きが出ないようにクギを刺した。（大嶽潤平、中山潤）【一覧】一目でわかる…過去に起きた「造反」に対する自民党の処分・対応
「処分はダラダラ遅くなるよりも早い方がいい。議論を尽くしたのに退席をするのは筋が通らない」
自民の鈴木幹事長は９日の役員会後の記者会見で、６日の衆院本会議での採決から間を置かずに処分を決めた理由をこう説明した。
自民では党則に基づく処分は、重い方から順に「除名」「離党の勧告」「選挙における非公認」など８種類ある。重い処分は党紀委員会を開くことが必要になるが、今回の「戒告」は２番目に軽い処分となり、幹事長の権限で決定できる。
党内では「離党勧告などの重い処分が妥当だ」（閣僚経験者）との声も出ていたが、党紀委に諮れば、処分の決定までに時間がかかることが想定されたため、党執行部は、すぐに処分を下せる戒告を選んだ。
与党は参院で、賛成を表明済みの日本保守党を含めても過半数に２議席足りない。無所属議員らの賛同を得て成立を目指すが、自民内から退席者や欠席者が出れば、可決のために取り込まなければならない議席数が増えることになる。
実際、参院自民内にも消費税減税に慎重な議員や党執行部と距離を置く議員がいる。参院幹部の危機感は強く、磯崎仁彦・参院国会対策委員長は「否決か可決かに直結する。そういうことがないよう対応してもらうのが妥当だ」と語り、４人への処分が必要だとの認識を示した。日本維新の会も自民内の足並みの乱れを懸念しており、９日の幹事長会談で維新の柴田幹事長が鈴木氏に「対応を注視している」と伝えた。
自民は過去の重要法案でも、退席者を戒告や厳重注意などとしてきた。

title: ホンダ 米オハイオ州に工場新設へ
body: 【メアリーズビル（米中西部オハイオ州）時事】ホンダは9日、約30億ドル（約4700億円）を投じて米中西部オハイオ州に完成車工場を新設すると発表した。【写真】SUV「CR－V」のHVを製造しているホンダの米国工場年間生産能力は24万台で、2029年の稼働を目指す。米国でのハイブリッド車（HV）需要拡大に対応する狙い。スポーツ用多目的車（SUV）を中心に生産するとみられる。新工場はホンダの完成車工場としては米国では6カ所目となる。完成後、北米でのホンダの生産能力は現在の年間167万台から同191万台に増加する。既存のイーストリバティ工場に隣接した敷地に建設。2000人以上の新規雇用創出につながるという。米国ホンダのボブ・ネルソン上級副社長は記者会見で「新工場はホンダの世界で最も先進的な工場の一つになる。柔軟性を重視し、ハイブリッド車、ガソリン車、電気自動車（EV）を生産する能力を備える」と強調。HVを重視しつつ、激しい市場環境の変化に対応可能な工場とする考えを示した。

title: 徳島・阿波市長ら 詐欺疑いで逮捕
body: 徳島県阿波市の市長が、市が発注したケーブルネットワーク事業に関する工事代金の中に、自身が起こした交通事故に伴う修理費用・350万円を上乗せしてだましとった疑いで逮捕されました。【動画ニュース】全国で相次ぐ迷惑行為「少林寺レーシング」詐欺の疑いで逮捕されたのは、阿波市長の町田寿人容疑者（69）ら３人です。町田容疑者らは、阿波市が民間企業との間で締結している市のケーブルネットワーク事業に関する工事代金の中に、町田容疑者が起こした交通事故に伴う修理費用・350万円を盛り込み騙し取った疑いが持たれています。

title: 室蘭殺人 男「騒音うるさかった」
body: 北海道室蘭市で11月6日、71歳の男性が死亡し、同じアパートの下の部屋に住む男が殺人の疑いで逮捕された事件で、男が「騒音がうるさかった」という趣旨の供述をしていることが捜査関係者への取材で分かりました。【続報】「窓から部屋をのぞいたり騒音もあるので注意して」逮捕の男…警察に通報も　男性が刃物で刺され死亡室蘭市の無職、在田実容疑者（74）は、11月6日午後8時20分ごろ、室蘭市高砂町の自宅アパートの共同廊下で、住人の谷一夫さん（71）を刃物で複数回刺し、殺害した疑いがもたれています。2人は同じアパートの住人で、在田容疑者は谷さんの部屋の真下に住んでいました。警察によりますと、谷さんの死因は胸や腹を刺されたことによる出血性ショックだったということです。その後の捜査関係者への取材で、在田容疑者が調べに対し「騒音がうるさかった」という趣旨の供述をしていることが分かりました。在田容疑者は刺したことは認めているものの「死なないと思った」と殺意を否認していて、警察が2人の間にトラブルがあったとみて調べています。

title: マンション2人死亡 7階から転落か
body: １１月９日夜、札幌市北区のマンションの敷地で男性２人が倒れているのが見つかり、その後、死亡が確認されました。【速報】マンション敷地で男性2人が倒れているのを発見　搬送先で死亡確認　事件の可能性も　札幌警察は、２人がマンションから転落したとみて捜査しています。ベランダの柵が壊れ、周りには血痕も残っています。札幌市北区あいの里３条６丁目のマンションで、９日午後８時２０分ごろ、「物音を聞いて見に行ったところ、男性２人が倒れていた」と消防に通報がありました。２人は１階の敷地で発見され、搬送先の病院で死亡が確認されました。警察によりますと、２人は７階に住む３０代～４０代くらいの家族とみられるということです。（同じマンションの住人）「何ともいえない人の声が一瞬聞こえて、ベランダから出たら、向かいの駐車場にいた方が、上から落ちたと言っていた」警察は、２人が７階の部屋から転落したとみて、事件の可能性も視野に捜査しています。

title: 米大統領 中露首脳と会談の見通し
body: ［８日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は８日、中国で来週開かれるアジア太平洋経済‌協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせ、中国の⁠習近平国家主席、ロシアのプーチン大統領と会談し、イランでの戦争終結や非核​化について協議することになるとの見通しを示した。トランプ氏はフロリダ‌州からワシントンに戻る前に記者団に対し、中国南部の深センで１８─１９日に開催されるＡＰＥＣ首脳会‌議出席のために訪‌中すると述べた。「会談の一つ​はプーチン大統領、習主席とのものになると思う。興‌味深いものになるだろう。非核化を含め、多くのことを話‌し合っているが、会談​でも幅広い議題を取り上げる。われ‌われはイランでの戦争終結を目指している」と語った。ト⁠ランプ氏は先月、習氏とプーチン氏との３者による軍備管理協議に前向きな姿勢を示し、非核化が焦点にな⁠ると述べていた。米紙ウォール・ス​トリート・ジ‌ャーナルはその後、プーチン氏が３者会談を利用し、長期化するロシアとウクライナの戦争終結に⁠ついて協議することを提案したと報じた。ト⁠ランプ氏は米ＣＢＳの番組「６０ミニッツ」のインタビューで、ロシア⁠とウクライナの戦争終結に向け「合意に非常に近づいてい‌ると⁠思う」と発言。合意によってウクライナ​は「少し違う形」になるとしたが、具体的な説明はしなかった。

title: MAGAから急進左派へ 揺らぐ米国
body:
関税戦争と物価高に苦しむ人々、トランプ支持から急進左派への転換、そして民主党内の対立。中間選挙の激戦州で見えたのは、共和党対民主党という単純な構図では説明できないアメリカの変化だった。【写真】エルサイード氏支持者が語る…その理由とは（ニューヨーク支局長　親松聖）デトロイトの街を歩くと、かつてアメリカの自動車産業を支えた工業都市の衰退の歴史が見える。製造業の空洞化や人口流出などに直面し、長く経済的な苦境が続いてきた「錆びついた工業地帯」ミシガン州・デトロイト。住民の暮らしをさらに圧迫しているのが、止まらない物価高だ。今回の中間選挙で、ミシガン州の上院選を制したのは、民主党の新星、アブドゥル・エルサイード氏だった。トランプ大統領の盟友である共和党のマイク・ロジャース氏を破り、イスラム教徒として初めての上院議員となる。エルサイード氏は公衆衛生の専門家で、急進左派的な政策を掲げている。イスラエルに対する厳しい立場を打ち出し、行き過ぎた資本主義の見直しを訴え、大企業や富裕層への増税、国民皆保険の実現など、有権者の暮らしに直結する政策を前面に打ち出し、支持を広げていった。今回、ミシガンを取材していて、多くの人々から聞こえてきたのは、ただでさえ苦しい生活に追い打ちをかけるガソリン高と、この地域特有のトランプ関税への怒りだった。
デトロイトは、川を挟んでカナダと接している。両国の経済が深く結びつく中、トランプ政権が仕掛けたカナダとの関税戦争が、地元企業の経営や人々の暮らしに大きな影を落としていた。その影響を直接受けていたのが、家具メーカー「Howard Family Designs」のオーナー、マイケル・ハワードさんだ。ハワードさんは、関税によって木材やアルミニウムなどの仕入れ価格が急上昇し、仕事の受注にも深刻な影響が出ているという。「カナダとの関税のせいで、あらゆるもののコストが大幅に上がり、木材やアルミは3倍近くになった。商品の値段を上げざるを得ないが、病院の受付カウンターやキャビネット、家庭向けのキッチンキャビネットなど、多くのプロジェクトが中止になり、仕事の量が劇的に減っている。妻や子供を支えることにも影響が出ている」売り上げが3割程度落ち込む中、ハワードさんは人員削減という苦渋の選択に踏み切った。「トランプ大統領は、関税はアメリカの企業や労働者を守るためのものだと言っていたが、これは全くの誤りだ。実際にはアメリカの企業を傷つけ、労働者を苦しめている。私たちは、雇用していた従業員を維持することができなくなってしまった」周囲にも、関税によるコストの高騰で、事業を続けていくこと自体が難しくなっていると感じる人が増えているという。「自分自身の判断が原因で事業が打撃を受けたのなら、そこから学び、成長し、改善していくことができます。しかし、現在私たちが受けている悪影響は、私たちとは何の関係もありません。すべてはトランプ大統領とその政権によるものなのです」ハワードさんは、こうした現状を変えてほしいと、急進左派のエルサイード氏に期待を寄せていた。「私は4人の子供の父親です。そのうち3人は現在学校に通っていますが、トランプ氏の関税のせいで、学用品の価格が30％も上がってしまいました。友人の一人は、医療保険料が3倍になったと電話で話していました。彼らにも子供がいるんです。医療費だけで月に2000ドルもかかり、その上、家賃や住居費も支払わなければならないとしたら、一体どうやって家族を養っていけばいいのでしょうか。ごく普通のアメリカ市民と向き合い、私たちにとって何が最も重要なのかを聞き、それらの問題にどう対処していくのか、具体的な計画を提示してほしい」トランプ大統領がアメリカの企業や労働者を守ると掲げた関税政策。しかし、現場で聞こえてきたのは、仕事を失い、家族の生活まで脅かされているという経営者の切実な声だった。

title: 米国防長官の弾劾採決へ 米下院
body: ［ワシントン　９日　ロイター］ - 米共和党のトーマス・マッシー下院議員は９日、連邦議会の承認なしにイランとの戦争を遂行したことや、職権乱用などの容疑を巡り、ヘグセス国防‌長官に対する８項目の弾劾訴追条項を提出した。マッシー氏は記者会見で、共和党指導部⁠が手続き上の動議によって弾劾訴追案を退け、直接の採決を回避しようとする可能性があると指摘。「彼らは、この問題の中身を問う採決を避けようとするかもしれない。われわれは、この８項目​の弾劾訴追条項について採決し、徹底的に議論すべきだ」と述べた。下院規則では２日以内に審理を行う必要があり、週内にも採決が行われる可能性がある。議会関係筋によると、‌決議案は、民主党が来年１月３日に主導権を握るまで共和党が多数を占める下院でも可決に必要な単純過半数を獲得する可能性があるという。ただ、上院での有罪認定には３分の２の賛成が必要で、共和党が１００議席‌のうち５３議席を占めているため、有罪となる可‌能性は低いとみられる。トランプ大統領は９日のロイターとのインタビューで、​ヘグセス長官を擁護する姿勢を示した。「２つの戦争に勝った彼をどうやって弾劾できるのか分からない」と述べ、ベトナム、ア‌フガニスタン、イラクなどで何年も戦争を続けて何の成果も出せなかった過去の責任者こそ弾劾すべきではないかと反論した。ジョンソン下院‌議長（共和党）は弾劾の動きに反対し、「​海外で武力衝突が続く中」での弾劾は「われわれの同盟国にとっても敵国にと‌っても見るに堪えないものになる」と述べた。ヘグセス氏が下院で弾劾訴追されれば、米軍を統括する文民としては１８７６年のウィリアム・⁠ベルナップ戦争長官以来となる。ベルナップ氏は巨額の賄賂を受け取ったとして辞表を提出。下院は辞任後も弾劾訴追し、上院では３分の２の賛成に届かず、無罪となった。＜ヘグセス氏「懸念していない」＞ヘグセス氏は９日、共和党内で弾劾訴追を阻止するのに⁠十分な支持を確保しているかとの質問に対し、「その点は懸念していな​い」と語った。１０日に国防総省で記者会見‌を開くことも明らかにした。同省での会見は５月以来となる。一部の共和党議員は、ヘグセス氏が留任すれば、議会との緊張関係がトランプ政権の目指す１兆５０００億ドルの国防支出計画の妨げになると懸念している。トランプ氏に批判的で、⁠来年１月に退任するマッシー氏は９日の声明で、弾劾は民主党が１月に議会の主導権を握った後にヘグ⁠セス氏を待ち受ける事態に比べれば「はるかに穏やか」なものだと警告した。「民主党は公聴会や裁判を開くだろう。トラン⁠プ大統領は、まだ上院で後任の承認を得られる今のうちに、ヘグセス長官を交代させるべきだ」と主張した。民主党は、統合参謀本部‌議長や他の軍⁠高官の解任などを巡り、ヘグセス氏を調査すると表明している。下院民主党のジェフリーズ院​内総務は８日、ヘグセス氏の弾劾訴追案に「断固として賛成」すると述べた。 また、上院民主党のシューマー院内総務も上院での審理が必要だと述べた。

title: 露政権批判の代表紙 編集部を閉鎖
body:
【モスクワ共同】ロシアのプーチン政権に批判的な調査報道を続けてきた同国の代表的な独立系メディアであるノーバヤ・ガゼータ紙は9日、モスクワの編集部を閉鎖した。当局からの圧力で資金源を断たれ、立ち退きを迫られたためだとし、1993年の創刊から30年超にわたる歴史にいったん幕を閉じた。【写真】「ロシア兵器9割に日本部品」　ミサイルや無人機に転用　名指しされた日本企業13社
同紙のソコロフ編集長は「現時点で新聞は存在しないが、記者もノーバヤ・ガゼータという理念も残る。『永遠にさようなら』と言うわけでなく、皆さんの元に戻ってくる」と述べ、将来的な復刊に含みを持たせた。一方、ロシアのペスコフ大統領報道官は9日「ロシア独立系メディアの時代が終わりを告げていると言うのは誤りだ」と述べ、当局による圧力を否定。ノーバヤ・ガゼータの廃刊はメディアの盛衰に伴う「入れ替わりの一環だ」と主張した。同紙の編集部では9日、2006年に射殺されたポリトコフスカヤ記者ら政権に批判的な報道などに取り組みながら殺害された6人の写真が壁から取り外された。

title: 仏大統領選 リネール氏が出馬表明
body: オリンピックで金メダルを5個獲得しているフランスの柔道家のテディ・リネール氏が、来年行われるフランス大統領選挙に出馬すると表明しました。【写真を見る】柔道家のテディ・リネール氏 国旗を背景に出馬表明フランスの柔道家のテディ・リネール氏（37）は自身のXで、来年行われるフランス大統領選挙に出馬すると表明しました。リネール氏はフランスを代表する柔道選手で、これまでオリンピックで金メダルを5個獲得。2024年のパリオリンピックでは、混合団体戦の決勝で日本と対戦した際に、引き分けで迎えた最後の試合の階級を決める「電子ルーレット」で、当時、絶対王者だったリネール選手の90キロ超級が選ばれて物議を醸しました。リネール氏はスーツ姿で国旗を背景に出馬表明し、「フランスのために闘いたい」と訴えました。テディ・リネール氏「フランスを立て直すための闘いは、上からではなく、皆さんとともに、皆さんのためのものです」フランス大統領選をめぐっては、最新の世論調査で極右「国民連合」のマリーヌ・ルペン氏が支持率およそ35％で首位に立っていて、急進左派「不服従のフランス」のメランション氏がおよそ18％と、ほかの候補をリードしています。

title: 個人向け国債人気 発行額8兆円超
body: 「金利ある世界」の本格到来で、個人向け国債の販売が好調だ。利回り上昇で投資妙味が増し、2026年度の発行額は既に8兆円を超え、過去最高を更新した。定期預金を大きく上回る利率が個人マネーを引き寄せ、銀行業界からは預金からの資金流出を警戒する声も出ている。【ひと目でわかる】日本国債の保有者別割合財務省によると、26年度の個人向け国債の発行額は、4～11月発行分までで8兆1896億円。既に昨年度を大きく上回り、過去最高だった05年度（7兆2712億円）を超えた。個人向け国債は現在、変動金利10年物と固定金利5年物、固定金利3年物の3種類。11月募集分では、固定5年物の利率は年2．17％。一方、定期預金の5年物の利息は大手行で年1％程度、ネット銀でも年2％に届かない。元本割れの心配はなく、高い利回りを狙える金融商品として人気が高まる。投資初心者向けの商品にも適し、証券会社は販売キャンペーンを展開する。SMBC日興証券は10月募集分で高額の購入に応じて現金を付与する特典を実施した。手島直樹本店長は「個人向け国債で投資が全て完結することはなく、資産運用を始めるきっかけになり得る」として、投資の「入り口」として期待する。本店の店頭では営業職員の提案に、80歳の男性投資家が「元本変動がないというのは初めて聞いた。銀行に置いておくよりはるかに良い」と耳を傾けていた。政府も個人向け国債の一段の販売促進に乗り出す。日銀が国債の買い入れ額を縮小する中、安定消化の受け皿として個人に期待する。財務省は商品性の拡充を検討。満期まで20年など超長期商品の導入や1万円からとなっている最低購入単位の引き下げなどが柱となる。27年度の税制改正要望には、財務省と金融庁が個人向け国債の優遇税制措置を盛り込んだ。与野党内では少額投資非課税制度（NISA）の対象に加える案や相続税減税案が浮上する。ただ、個人向け国債の優遇措置に危機感を強めるのが、銀行業界だ。貸し出しの原資となる預金の獲得競争が激しくなる中、個人向け国債への資金流出が進めば、銀行経営を圧迫しかねない。全国銀行協会の加藤勝彦会長（みずほ銀行頭取）は「資金シフトが過度に進むとニーズが高まっている成長資金の供給に影響が出る」と懸念を示している。

title: ホンダ 米オハイオ州に工場新設へ
body: 【メアリーズビル（米中西部オハイオ州）時事】ホンダは9日、約30億ドル（約4700億円）を投じて米中西部オハイオ州に完成車工場を新設すると発表した。【写真】SUV「CR－V」のHVを製造しているホンダの米国工場年間生産能力は24万台で、2029年の稼働を目指す。米国でのハイブリッド車（HV）需要拡大に対応する狙い。スポーツ用多目的車（SUV）を中心に生産するとみられる。新工場はホンダの完成車工場としては米国では6カ所目となる。完成後、北米でのホンダの生産能力は現在の年間167万台から同191万台に増加する。既存のイーストリバティ工場に隣接した敷地に建設。2000人以上の新規雇用創出につながるという。米国ホンダのボブ・ネルソン上級副社長は記者会見で「新工場はホンダの世界で最も先進的な工場の一つになる。柔軟性を重視し、ハイブリッド車、ガソリン車、電気自動車（EV）を生産する能力を備える」と強調。HVを重視しつつ、激しい市場環境の変化に対応可能な工場とする考えを示した。

title: 麻生コンクリ JIS認証取り消し
body: 福岡県の企業群、麻生グループの麻生コンクリート工業（福岡県粕屋町、清原定之社長）が、計画とは異なる種類のセメントを混合した生コンクリートを製造・出荷していた問題で、JIS（日本産業規格）登録認証機関の日本建築総合試験所（日総試）は11月9日、同社に対する認証を取り消した。報告を受けた経済産業省が同日発表した。【写真】麻生コンクリート工業がホームページに掲載した説明文経産省によると、日総試は麻生コンクリート工業の関係者から、JISで求める品質管理体制基準に適合しない取り扱いが行われていたと報告を受け、10月22日に現地調査を実施。長期間にわたり購入者に提出した計画書と異なる配合で製造・出荷し、これを隠蔽（いんぺい）するために記録を改ざんしていた事実を確認した。「品質管理体制に関する基準を満たしておらず、不適合の内容が重大」と判断したという。ただ、安全性への影響については判断していない。麻生コンクリート工業はこの問題で、9月12日から生コンクリートの出荷を停止。国土交通省九州地方整備局によると、建築物の安全性への影響などについては、麻生コンクリート工業などが確認を続けているという。

title: NTT 保有するNEC全株売却を発表
body: [東京 ９日 ロイター] - ＮＴＴは９日、保有する日本電気株（‌所有割合４．９０％）の全株⁠を売却すると発表した。半分をＮＥＣによる自社​株買いに応募し、残りを主に海外の‌投資家へ売却する。業務提携は継続‌する。ＮＴＴは２０２０年にＮＥＣ株約４．８％を約６４４億円で‌取得し、業務​資本提携を結んだ。光電融‌合技術による新たな情報通信基‌盤「ＩＯＷＮ（ア​イオン）」の開発‌などに共同で取り組んでき⁠たが、資本関係がなくても業務提携を拡大する関⁠係が構築でき​たと判断‌した。ＮＥＣはこのうちの半数に当たる２．４５％を１株３４６２円で公開買い付け（ＴＯＢ）す⁠る。取得上限額は１３００億円。１３日⁠から１２月１４日まで買い付ける。残る半数⁠は１２日に証券会社を介して主‌に海⁠外の機関投資家へ​売却する。売却価格は１０日に決める。

title: 火葬料 公営と民間で大きな差
body:
厚生労働省の研究班が実施した全国の火葬場を対象とした実態調査で、回答した有料施設の火葬料の平均が約１万４０００円だったことがわかった。大半が公営で、無料の施設も約２割あった。民間企業が運営する東京２３区の火葬場では８万円以上の費用がかかり、公費で住民負担を軽減している公営施設との差が浮き彫りとなった。（高田結奈、美根京子）【グラフ】住民の火葬は「無料」の施設の割合
「２３区の火葬場の料金がそんなに高いとは知らなかった」。昨年７月に父親（当時７８歳）を亡くした東京都江東区の女性（４６）は、葬儀を振り返って漏らした。
父は２３区内の民間施設で火葬され、その料金として９万円を支払った。父をみとると悲しみにくれる間もなく葬儀の準備に忙殺され、女性は「火葬場の料金を比較する余裕などなかった」と語る。
他地域の公設の火葬場では無料や安価に済むと知り、不公平さを感じる。女性は「２３区に住んでいるだけで、高額な火葬料を支払う現状には納得できない。国や自治体が地域格差の解消に動いてくれないものか」と訴える。
厚労省研究班は昨年８～９月、全国１３９２の火葬場（うち公設１３４３施設）を対象に火葬料などについての調査を行い、計３７８施設が回答した。結果によると、３１２施設（８２・５％）が住民の火葬料として９万～２０００円を徴収していた一方、６６施設（１７・５％）は無料としていた。有料施設の平均額は１万４２９１円だった。
最高額の９万円は東京２３区にある民間火葬場だった。２３区の全９か所の火葬場のうち、企業が運営する７施設は、一部葬祭業者の利用者に割引が適用される例を除き、火葬料をいずれも８万円以上としている。
厚労省などによると、企業が運営する火葬場は、２３区の７か所以外に全国で６施設ある。６施設に確認したところ、松山市の火葬場が約４万～８０００円としている以外は、いずれも約６万円以上で、民間施設の料金の高さが際立っている。

title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
body:
"He's suffering": Trump answers BBC question about Nvidia's Jensen Huang
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.
"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about$250bn (£190bn) off its valueon Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%.
Trump later told reporters at the White House that the FBI was looking into the issue, but did not elaborate on the investigation, or when it was launched. The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC.
US intelligence officials believeAlice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang.
According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage.
The American firm, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating Nvidia's exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns.
Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy.
The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China."
The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment on the lawsuit.
At the White House, Trump was asked several times, including by the BBC, when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific.
Trump said he thought that Huang was an "honourable guy and I feel very confident that he will be in good shape" after the investigations.
"I hope there's no problem, I believe he is suffering greatly," the president added.
He said he spoke to Huang on the phone on Monday "just to see if he's feeling alright, how you doing, and I asked him about that and he said he absolutely had no idea that the person in question was a spy".
Trump has raised concerns that allowing China to lead in AI would supercharge Beijing's military and surveillance capabilities.
The president added he was "sure" Chinese leader Xi Jinping would "ask me about it" when they next met.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Huang has admitted that he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
He said on Monday that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation the company had launched.
Huang has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week, however it is unclear whether Huang will appear.
A letter said the briefing would be "on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang".
Nvidia has declined to comment, while the the BBC has also contacted the committees.
Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
Some workers the BBC spoke to at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters on Monday said it was business as usual, despite the intense attention on the company.
Nvidia has been around for decades, with Huang founding it with two other engineers in 1993, but its rise to one of the world's most valuable and powerful companies has only been recent.
It originally designed computer chips for gaming, but its decision to shift focus to AI development turned it into the powerhouse it is today.
Its chips have become so valuable to the AI buildout that the White House previously imposed controls on where its advanced products could be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Huang has long been against restricting sales to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Nvidia's most advanced AI semiconductors including the GB200 Blackwell super chip remain blocked from the Chinese market.

title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
body:
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmakerannounced an independent investigationwould be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing,according to a New York Times report,external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.
Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.
"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk."
After Nvidia's investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang to continue leading the firm.
US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened the week on a positive note after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.
But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so important to the AI industry.
"Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but he decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Jensen Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
Jensen Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.
Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Jensen Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future."
The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched.
Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Jensen Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

title: Ukraine peace talks resume with 'some flexibility' by warring sides, US officials say
summary: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
body:
The talks come as Ukraine reels from a deadly Russian strike on a village in Zaporizhzhia last week, in which at least 40 people were killed
Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said.
The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February.
Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches.
Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.
"An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X.
But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart.
A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia.
Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security.
While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".
However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".
"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."
For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans.
The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are part of the US delegation that will attend the talks in Abu Dhabi
The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since.
Since then, European leaders - who have been largely excluded from peace talks – have pushed to be involved in the process amid concerns that decisions about the security of their continent would be made without them.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged on Monday to include Nato allies and EU members into any "meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture". President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated Kyiv wanted Europe to be part of the talks.
The US official said the Americans would propose moving into a multilateral format bringing the Europeans into the discussion. "Hopefully we'll get the Russians on board," the official said, while acknowledging that "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans."
Since the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success.
Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union.
After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine which "might involve all of Europe".
Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result into a fair peace.
Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believes Trump wants "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv.
The only way to make Putin start real negotiations is by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said.
"While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war".
Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi will include Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky.
Kyiv is sending several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya.
Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms.
On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations."
"This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism."

title: Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily with further strikes unlikely
summary: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation in the Middle East change.
body:
Trump: Iran militarily is "effectively over" and war ending "fairly soon"
Donald Trump says the Iran war "militarily is effectively over" declaring that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict.
"We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday.  "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."
Addressing reporters from the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change.
Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubts about the US president's prior comments about resolving the conflict.
Responding to a question over why he would not officially declare an end to the conflict, Trump said that some of the Gulf allies could still face Iranian aggression.
"We have some great allies there and we have to make sure they're not hurt," Trump said, suggesting that the US naval blockade on Iranian ports was helping to make the region more secure.
Trump hosted Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani in the Oval Office earlier on Monday, saying they had an "excellent conversation" about negotiations to end the war.
In a post on X, the Qatari prime minister said he held "positive discussions" with Trump and Vice-President JD Vance on "reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region".
Efforts to broker a peace between Washington and Tehran have largely been held indirectly through mediators since the war first broke out following joint US-Israeli strikes in February.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar and United Arab Emirates are among the US's Gulf allies that have been hit by Iranian strikes over the course of the war, in addition to threat of strikes that have led to major air travel disruptions in the region.
This is not the first time that Trump has said Iran war is "militarily" over, but the circumstances for him are different now.
Trump has hinted at de-escalation in Iran after a bruising set of midterm election results for the Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President Vance blamed on the Iran War.
In an interview with 60 minutes that aired on Sunday, the president said he did not currently see "any reason" to escalate the war.
Ahead of the midterms, Trump said US forces conducted what he described as "minor strikes" on anIranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Post-election recriminations over the US war in Iran are already placing pressure on members of the Trump administration.
Republican congressman Thomas Massie launched a strong attack against Trump's Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over the war in Iran, requesting a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach him.
Trump has backed Hegseth, who says he is "not worried" about the looming impeachment threats, calling Massie's effort a "sham".
While the move is unlikely to succeed with Republicans still in control of Congress until January, Democrats have expressed willingness to impeach Hegseth once the new session begins and they have control of both the House and the Senate.

title: Epstein associate who still runs model agency 'put me in danger' says abuse survivor
summary: A woman says an agency boss sent her to photoshoots at the sex offender's Florida beach home.
body:
Roza has decided to share her story with the BBC
A woman raped by Jeffrey Epstein says the president of the model agency representing her put her in danger, when he sent her to two photoshoots at the convicted sex offender's Florida beach house.
At the time, in 2009, Epstein was serving a jail sentence for sex offences against a minor but was allowed to work each day from his home.
"My agency's job was to protect me, and they failed. In fact, they put me in danger. And for that, they should be held accountable," she tells the BBC World Service.
Roza was 18 when she was first sent to Epstein's Palm Beach home by MC2 Model Management's US branch, having only arrived in the US from Uzbekistan about a month earlier. MC2's US president at the time, Jeff Fuller, now runs another US model agency called The Source Models.
"My agency knew exactly where I was. So Jeff knew exactly where I was going," says Roza.
Jeff Fuller now runs The Source Models agency
She shows us an expense statement suggesting Fuller himself booked her flight home from Palm Beach, following her second shoot at Epstein's home. Fuller has previously claimed he did not know Roza was going to Epstein's house.
She says the photoshoots led to her being employed as an assistant to Epstein. Other survivors have explained how the financier used the recruitment of assistants asan elaborate ruse to allow him to continue abusing young women.
Roza says Epstein went on to systematically rape her.
Fuller has not responded to the BBC's allegations. He has previously said he did not know Roza was being abused.
We discovered through the Epstein-related documents released by the US Department of Justice [DOJ] that 10 models from MC2 met, or were in communication with, Epstein after his conviction.
The files also show Epstein gave $1m (£742,000) to MC2 in 2005 - despite the agency owners telling a US publication two years later that Epstein had no involvement in their company.
Testimony shared with BBC Eye also raises questions about the role played by two other individuals who were active in the model industry, and whom the DOJ files show had close relationships with Epstein - former agent Ramsey Elkholy and agency director Faith Kates.
A DOJ statement from last year, that no evidence has been uncovered which would warrant further investigation against "uncharged third parties", is now being challenged by New York State senator, Zellnor Myrie.
He has proposed a new sex trafficking bill to give police greater power to investigate Epstein's alleged enablers.
Senator Myrie told the BBC he wants those who knew - or should have known - about Epstein's abuse to be held accountable
Sara Ziff, founder of the Model Alliance, which campaigns for stronger protections for models in the US, approves.
"Often, [model agencies] are the problem. They are the link between the model and these predatory men."
Roza says the person behind the camera at the photoshoots MC2 sent her to was not a professional photographer, but Epstein's girlfriend at the time,Nadia Marcinko.
Roza describes the set-up as "strange - there was no stylist" and the photos were never used. She has since become convinced the shoots were stage-managed by Epstein and MC2.
BBC Eye reveals new evidence showing how scouts, agencies and powerful fashion figures helped Jeffrey Epstein gain access to young women after his conviction for sex offences.
If you are outside the UK, pleasewatch on YouTube,external
An email in the DOJ files, from Fuller to Epstein, makes clear the close ties between the agency and the financier.
"Had it not been for you, we would have fired her months ago," Fuller writes of another model in March 2012. "And I would be careful as she blabs about things," he says.
A month after Epstein's second arrest in 2019, MC2's US branch was dissolved and Fuller opened a new agency, The Source Models, which is still operating. The BBC has found that 50 models from MC2 were transferred to his new agency.
We asked The Source Models to comment on our findings - it did not reply.
Model agencies were useful to Epstein, says Sigrid McCawley, the lead lawyer for more than 100 of Epstein's victims.
"Epstein said to many people he wanted three different girls a day. Think about those numbers... The [model] scouts were really critical because they were the ones who were identifying the type of woman that Epstein liked."
In the case of former agent Ramsey Elkholy, BBC Eye has discovered he tried to connect 34 women to Epstein, including an 18-year-old who was still in school.
The experience of one of the women highlights how assistants would be co-opted into the structure of the abuse.
Elkholy, the DOJ files show, suggested to Epstein that one of the financier's female assistants befriend this woman, before introducing her to Epstein.
We spoke to this woman, and she revealed that at her first meeting with Epstein, aged 19, he sexually abused her in his New York townhouse.
Ramsey Elkholy told the BBC: "I completely reject any allegation that I knew of or facilitated abuse of any kind… At the time, I had no knowledge of any abuse and I knew only his own [Epstein's] account of his 2008 [legal] case, which I misguidedly believed."
He continued: "The record and published reporting show that women were often groomed by other women in his inner circle. I was never part of that circle, or indeed of any such activity… my intention was to help models find professional opportunities by introducing them to an extremely well-connected individual."
If you are in the UK and you have been affected by any of the issues in this story such assexual abuse and violence, information and support is available atBBC Action Line
Lawyer Sigrid McCawley says these female assistants would have had "no choice" in how they conducted themselves.
"These young survivors were being abused regularly. Their livelihoods were being threatened… They had to do what they were being told to do."
Another model we have spoken to, Simona (not her real name), from eastern Europe, told us Epstein had raped her more than 200 times.
"People think that we gained something, that we agreed on this abuse in order to gain something, whether it's monetary or influential, but it's not true. We're left with deep trauma," says Simona.
She says the first time she met the financier, aged 20, she was already signed with a model agency in New York, and he offered to introduce her to his "good" friend Faith Kates.
At the time, Kates was the head of Next Management, one of the world's biggest model agencies. She stepped down from that senior executive position in December last year, but is still legally listed as a director of the company.
Simona says Faith Kates, pictured here, met her at Epstein's request
Simona says at this meeting, Kates suggested she undergo plastic surgery and sent details of a surgeon to Epstein.
After her meeting with Kates, Simona says Epstein convinced her to stop modelling.
And just like Roza, and several other of his victims, she became his assistant. She says he went on to rape her and control every aspect of her life for nearly two years.
The DOJ files show Epstein asked Kates to meet an additional five models, though it is not clear how many of these meetings took place.
Lawyers for Faith Kates told the BBC: "Jeffrey Epstein was a master manipulator... Ms Kates was one of those grossly misled by Epstein. Had she known then what she - and everyone else - now knows, she would have never associated with him."
They added she had never asked a model to have plastic surgery.
We approached Next Management for comment, but it did not reply.
Myrie told the BBC that if his bill were to become law, and "you were sending models to Epstein and you knew what Epstein was doing, or you should have known what he was doing, you will be held accountable".
Roza hopes sharing her story will encourage others to come forward.
"There are many, many survivors out there who never speak, because it's scary. So to all my sister survivors… you know me now. You know my name. I say, reach out."
Additional reporting by Annika Grosser

title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
body:
"He's suffering": Trump answers BBC question about Nvidia's Jensen Huang
US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.
"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia, which has commissioned an independent investigation into the affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy, said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised.
Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company after Apple, and designs computer chips that have become central to AI technology. The revelations knocked about$250bn (£190bn) off its valueon Monday as the company's share price fell by more than 4%.
Trump later told reporters at the White House that the FBI was looking into the issue, but did not elaborate on the investigation, or when it was launched. The FBI declined to comment when contacted by the BBC.
US intelligence officials believeAlice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. She is not related to Jensen Huang.
According to the newspaper, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring, warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Trump's remarks are the first indication of whether Nvidia's Huang knew about the woman's alleged ties to Chinese espionage.
The American firm, co-founded by Jensen Huang, is also a major focus in the AI technology race between the US and China, with officials in Washington treating Nvidia's exports to Beijing as a matter of national security - a key reason why Huang's affair has sparked concerns.
Also on Monday, Huang and Nvidia were sued in a proposed class action lawsuit in California that accuses them of defrauding shareholders by concealing his ties with the suspected Chinese spy.
The lawsuit alleges that the company lied to the media about Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, "who is suspected of seeking to help smuggle Nvidia products to China."
The BBC has contacted Nvidia for comment on the lawsuit.
At the White House, Trump was asked several times, including by the BBC, when he was made aware of the relationship. He said he was informed "over a period of time" but was not specific.
Trump said he thought that Huang was an "honourable guy and I feel very confident that he will be in good shape" after the investigations.
"I hope there's no problem, I believe he is suffering greatly," the president added.
He said he spoke to Huang on the phone on Monday "just to see if he's feeling alright, how you doing, and I asked him about that and he said he absolutely had no idea that the person in question was a spy".
Trump has raised concerns that allowing China to lead in AI would supercharge Beijing's military and surveillance capabilities.
The president added he was "sure" Chinese leader Xi Jinping would "ask me about it" when they next met.
Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?
Huang has admitted that he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
He said on Monday that he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation the company had launched.
Huang has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week, however it is unclear whether Huang will appear.
A letter said the briefing would be "on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People's Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang".
Nvidia has declined to comment, while the the BBC has also contacted the committees.

Some workers the BBC spoke to at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters on Monday said it was business as usual, despite the intense attention on the company.
Nvidia has been around for decades, with Huang founding it with two other engineers in 1993, but its rise to one of the world's most valuable and powerful companies has only been recent.
It originally designed computer chips for gaming, but its decision to shift focus to AI development turned it into the powerhouse it is today.
Its chips have become so valuable to the AI buildout that the White House previously imposed controls on where its advanced products could be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Huang has long been against restricting sales to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Nvidia's most advanced AI semiconductors including the GB200 Blackwell super chip remain blocked from the Chinese market.

title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
body:
Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmakerannounced an independent investigationwould be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing,according to a New York Times report,external.
The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.
Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.
"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk."
After Nvidia's investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang to continue leading the firm.
US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened the week on a positive note after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.
But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived. Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so important to the AI industry.
"Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but he decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Jensen Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
Jensen Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.
Fernandez said she does not believe the board will remove Jensen Huang as chief executive, unless there is glaring evidence of wrongdoing related to national security or intellectual property, "but I bet they start bringing someone up as his number two, to have there for the future."
The modest fall in its shares mean investors believe it is unlikely he will step down or be removed as chief executive, but that the outcome of the investigation will be closely watched.
Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value. Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
But Jensen Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
Additional reporter by Samira Hussain, North America business correspondent.

title: Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
summary: Jensen Huang is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
body:
Jensen Huang, 63, has been called the 'Taylor Swift of tech' in the US
The tech world has spent the day digesting the extraordinary news that Jensen Huang - the charismatic, leather-jacket wearing chief executive of the multi-trillion dollar firm Nvidia - is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
None of us had that on our bingo cards for 2026.
Huang's alleged romantic affair with Alice Huang (no relation), the former CEO of a Singapore-based data centre company, has cast ripples far beyond his immediate family - undoubtedly on an emotional rollercoaster of their own - taking us to a crossroads at which technology, geopolitics and national security intersect.
In a nutshell, this is about the bitter rivalry between the US and China, as well as whether Jensen Huang has betrayed the US as well as his wife.
"He's suffering": Trump answers BBC question about Nvidia's Jensen Huang
The US is locked in a fierce race with China to develop the best AI models.
"Whoever wins AI, wins," as US President Donald Trump puts it. He thinks that the country with the more dominant AI technology will benefit the most from it and, ultimately, will be the most powerful in the world. He may well be right.
Nvidia happens to make the best chips in the business for AI – so much so that it has been overwhelmed with demand.
It sets its prices accordingly: a single unit of the firm's latest kit for data centres starts at £37,000 ($50,000). A medium or large site might have hundreds of them.
The US administration initially slapped an export ban on Nvidia's more recent devices to prevent China from taking advantage of their superior capabilities. It has since softened the rules a little.
But there are suggestions that Alice Huang's company, Megaspeed, may have been involved in sneaking them into the country while she was in charge. Bloomberg reported that the firm bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia tech in November 2025. Megaspeed denies that it was used illegitimately.
For his part, Jensen Huang has lobbied heavily for the export rules between the two countries to be relaxed, arguing against the weight of general opinion that the AI race doesn't matter and that it would be no bad thing for China to become dependent on US tech.
"President Trump wants American to win and President Xi wants China to win, and it's possible for both of them to do so," he told the BBC last year.
It think it's safe to assume that neither country sees it that way.
Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
Could this be the end of 'Jensanity'
The difficult questions Nvidia now has to try to answer include whether Alice gained special access to the firm's latest technology, either deliberately or not, via Jensen - and, if so, whether she shared it with Beijing or others.
We don't know when their affair began or ended, but there are numerous photos and videos of Jensen and Alice together at events. It is feasible that there were moments when they spent quite a lot of time together and Jensen has talked about always having an eye on his work.
China denies that she was engaged in espionage.
Interest in economic espionage is neither new nor unique to China. But many Western countries say that China does it on a grand scale, using a combination of technology tools and agents embedded in various organisations - including private companies.
China having access to significant enough numbers of Nvidia's chips to make use of them, or stripping them down and learning how to make its own versions, would infuriate the Trump administration, which is trying to keep its AI technology close to its chest.
Some models have even been withheld from the UK-based AI Safety Institute on the grounds that they are potentially too dangerous to be shared. The US does not want anyone having a headstart or misusing its innovations.
Another potential bombshell lies in the form of any national security information to which Jensen Huang may have been privy.
He is a man operating at the very top of the US elite - one of a handful of people who could probably walk into the White House unannounced and have tea with Trump. He has influence, he has access and he has powerful friends. It's quite possible that secrets were shared with him.
Nvidia says there's no evidence so far that he passed anything on and the firm has launched an internal investigation. Huang says he will co-operate and wants to keep his job - though if nothing else, he has broken Nvidia's own code of conduct, which states that company members should not have relationships with clients.
At present, he has the backing of both the Nvidia board and Trump, whodescribed him as "honourable"and speculated that there must have been a reason for what had transpired. In other words, he's not throwing his tech boss buddy under the bus.
Nvidia's share price has fallen but has not tanked spectacularly, suggesting shareholders are not abandoning the company under his stewardship in their droves either.
An AI industry with a weakened Nvidia would undoubtedly be a slower one.
And there isn't really a natural successor waiting in the wings to replace Jensen were he forced out.
Huang has run Nvidia for more than 30 years - to many, he is Nvidia. He has steered it through multiple crises and it was his decision for the firm to focus on AI before it was trendy.
He is known to be a demanding boss who expects staff to work long hours and to high standards. There are stories about him calling all-staff meetings to tell off individuals who had made mistakes. He has said this was to prevent others making the same errors – but you can only imagine how it felt for those on the receiving end.
While he awaits the conclusion of the investigation into his actions, Huang must hope that, despite not tolerating the mistakes of his colleagues in the past, they will be gracious about his own failings.
And he must also live with the irony that he was potentially caught out not by a sophisticated high-tech sting, but by the oldest trick in the book: a honey trap.

title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
body:
Civil servant Kashim Chowdhury juggled multiple public sector jobs
A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud.
Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money.
The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''.
After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose.
The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing.
"This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty," said Sarah Melo, specialist prosecutor at the CPS Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate.
"He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing."
A Defra spokesperson said Chowdury "abused the trust placed in him as a public servant", adding that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending.
The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''
Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped and earned him £350,000 in total.
The prosecution told the court that on application forms he provided inaccurate information about his employment status and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already a civil servant. Once he secured the roles he didn't tell his employers he was working elsewhere.
He was allowed to work entirely from home because he told his employers he was caring for his mother, whom he lived with in east London. She had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023.
How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
But rather than reduce his workload to look after her, he kept taking on new jobs. In the spring of 2023, when his mother was a few months away from death, he had jobs at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office.
During this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days.
Chowdhury said he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment in the past. He was made redundant from a job at the Department for Education in 2013 and was given a diagnosis of PTSD.
He said he had not been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time".
But the prosecution barrister, Lucy Organ, told the jury: "He's lied to you in evidence, he's lied to you under oath, which demonstrates the level of deceit he has descended to."
A succession of his managers told the court about his poor performance. Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney who managed Chowdhury at Defra.
He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time". McCartney said that during video calls Chowdhury had his camera switched off blaming technical problems. McCartney said this went on for four to five months.
But McCartney said that because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job and remained there for two years.
Chowdhury told the jury he had not worn make-up during a work video call
The prosecution argued that he used sick notes to cope with his impossible schedule. In March 2023, he was on sick leave from four of the organisations he worked for. But he kept working at the Home Office and did not tell them he was ill.
His line manager at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023. By this point he'd been off sick for three months and she wanted to make a plan to get him back to work.
She told the jury that at the start of the call he was coughing a lot and waving tissues up to the camera. She also told the jury that he had been wearing white make-up to try to look ill.
Adams told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck."
Chowdhury told the jury this was a smear and that he had not been wearing make-up.
After the call, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it he blamed a technical error.
Adams grew suspicious. ''I believed he was lying,'' she told the jury. She escalated her concerns up the chain at the UKHSA.
But his fraudulent behaviour went on for several more months until he left the civil service in September 2023.
He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of civil service databases such as payroll every two years to look for anomalies.
Chowdhury has also been accused by his siblings of bullying their mother into increasing his share of the family home days before she died.
In a case at the High Court, Chowdhury's two brothers and sister allege that he put "undue influence" on Faijun Nessa to sign documents that meant he would inherit half of her home.
The four-storey, six-bedroom home in east London has been valued at £2.1m.
His siblings say their mother could not have understood what she was signing because she was "desperately unwell". In January 2023 she was given a terminal diagnosis of stage four metastatic colorectal cancer.
The claimants also allege that Mrs Nessa, who was nearly blind and could not speak English, was unaware of what she was signing because the documents were not translated into her native Bengali at the time they were signed.
Kashim Chowdhury denies the claims. That case is ongoing.

title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
summary: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
body:
Kashim Chowdhury fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money
Aleesha Adams joined a video call with Kashim Chowdhury in May 2023.
He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work.
At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked.
She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial.
She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court.
Little did she know UKHSA was not Chowdhury's only employer.
That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. He was contracted to work 183 hours a week – more than the number of hours in seven days. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money.
In total, he had eight overlapping full-time public-sector jobs between 2020 and 2023. During that time, this relatively junior civil servant was paid £350,000.
Soon after her call with Chowdhury, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address. When she challenged him about it, he blamed it on a technical error. She told the jury at his trial at Southwark Crown Court: "I believed he was lying." She escalated her concerns up the chain.
But his fraudulent behaviour remained undetected. Chowdhury was able to keep working multiple government jobs until September 2023 when he left the Civil Service.
He was finally caught in 2024 by the government's National Fraud Initiative, which conducts searches of Civil Service databases, such as payroll, every two years to look for anomalies.
On Monday he was found guilty of nine counts of fraud and told by the judge that he would be facing a "very substantial custodial sentence".
Chowdhury, 56, arrived each day at court alone. He is married, yet there never seemed to be any friends or family there to support him.
He would often make his way down the corridors of the court building carrying two plastic carrier bags, with a bobble hat perched on his head.
He sometimes looked bewildered in the witness box.
Chowdhury, who had a diagnosis of PTSD in 2015, said that he had taken on so many roles because he feared losing his livelihood after experiencing insecure employment. He said he'd been forced out of a job at the Department for Education in 2013.
He said he hadn't been thinking clearly when applying for jobs ''because of my stress, distress and trauma and due to my panic at the time".
But the prosecution argued his behaviour was "deliberate" and "intentional dishonesty" and that he had exploited the system.
Chowdhury sometimes looked bewildered in the witness box
However, the case raises important questions for the Civil Service. How was he able to get away with it for so long?
Part of the explanation is that the Civil Service's human resources system is not centralised. Chowdhury did not declare on government application forms that he was already a civil servant, so the system did not spot the duplication.
Hannah Keenan, who works at the Institute for Government, says the system clearly failed. "Government departments are taking hiring decisions independently of each other and without systems that join up," she said.
"That the model and the culture surrounding it aren't working shouldn't be a surprise though - we've known for a long time about poor performers flying under the radar by shuffling between jobs."
There are more than 550,000 people employed across the Civil Service, many in offices in Whitehall, in central London. They are responsible for carrying out government policy and the daily administration of the country.
Another reason why Chowdhury's fraud went undetected is that he was working entirely from the east London house he shared with his mother. In 2023, she had dementia and terminal cancer, and he told his employers that he needed to be at home to look after her.
But rather than reducing his workload to concentrate on her care, he took on more jobs. He covered up his impossible daily schedule by getting sick notes from his GP.
In April 2023, he was off with what he called "mixed anxiety and depressive disorder" from Defra, the UKHSA, the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency.
While the sick notes were shown to the jury, they were not given evidence about what caused the depressive disorder or of a psychiatric assessment having been done during this period.
His sickness did not prevent him from starting yet another job – this time at the Home Office. He did not mention to them he was ill, nor did he tell them he was working elsewhere.
Unsurprisingly, a succession of his line managers told the jury he had not been very good at his jobs.
Especially damning was the evidence given by Dan McCartney, who managed Chowdhury at Defra. He said he had to "effectively tell him what to do the whole time" and that Chowdhury kept his camera off during video calls for four months, claiming technical problems.
But because Chowdhury was not subject to any formal performance measures at Defra, he was given a permanent job. He remained there for two years.
In September 2023, Chowdhury was found to have more than £40,000 in his bank accounts as well as significant investments, including £45,000 in premium bonds.
A recent survey of 1,700 civil servants by the independent think tank Re:State found 76% of respondents thought it did not do a good job of tackling poor performers.
An ex-senior civil servant told the BBC that much of the Civil Service is culturally averse to performance management.
"Whitehall's known for ages it has to be less risk averse. Shrinking the Civil Service and the adoption of artificial intelligence technology make that more vital," they said.
"But don't underestimate the fear factor: fear of drawn-out grievances and fear of being accused of wasting taxpayers' money if the Civil Service was to do what big private sector firms do, which is cut to get rid of poor performers by offering some money and a settlement agreement."
A Defra spokesperson said: "Kashim Chowdhury abused the trust placed in him as a public servant and defrauded taxpayers out of almost £285,000. He will now rightly face the consequences for his actions.
"This conviction is the result of a thorough and painstaking investigation led by the Defra Counter Fraud and Investigations team. It sends a clear message that fraud against the public purse will not be tolerated and those responsible will be held to account."
The spokesperson said Defra would use "all available avenues to recover the proceeds of Chowdhury's offending on behalf of taxpayers".
Chowdhury's case also illustrates a wider issue.
He was engaged in what is being called "polygamous working", where people hold down several jobs secretly. Websites have even been set up offering people advice on how to keep their employers in the dark.
Its rise has been blamed on larger numbers of people working from home.
The government's National Fraud Initiative has identified 23 cases of "polygamous working" across London in its most recent report. It uncovered £500,000 of overpaid salaries over a period of a few months.
Alongside the fraud case, Chowdhury is involved in a legal dispute with his three siblings, who accuse him of ''bullying'' their mother into signing over half of her £2.1m home to him in the final days of her life. He denies it.
At times during his criminal trial, Chowdhury appeared confused by what he was hearing and blamed trauma for the web of lies he had spun. The jury took seven hours to reach their verdict and decided he was motivated by personal gain - stealing tens of thousands of pounds from the taxpayer.
Chowdhury now faces a significant custodial sentence.

title: Action on energy costs is my overriding aim, says Fahnbulleh
summary: The energy secretary says reducing bills is key to maintaining public support for climate action.
body:
The energy secretary has stressed that affordability is her "overriding objective", as she said reducing bills would be key to maintaining public support for climate action.
Speaking to BBC Panorama, Miatta Fahnbulleh insisted that the government's drive for cleaner power would help to cut energy bills in the long term.
But she conceded that the push to reduce carbon emissions was currently "under pressure" amid discontent at rising prices in recent years.
It comes as ministers grapple with how to respond to a predicted surge in energy prices in January, expected to mark the biggest rise in bills for four years.
Scientists predict 2026 hottest year on record as climate talks begin
Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
Labour has faced extra political pressure over its climate ambitions since coming to power, as Reform UK rose in opinion polls and the Conservatives under Kemi Badenochdisowned their previous ambitionof reaching net zero by 2050.
Both opposition parties have taken particular aim at public subsidy schemes designed to boost renewable sources of electricity generation, arguing that the drive for cleaner energy has driven up costs for consumers.
UK households currently pay one of the highest rates for electricity in Europe.
Bills have increased due to subsidies but also because of the high price of gas (a fossil fuel) driven up by international conflicts.
Three reasons why UK electricity prices are so high
Asked during her Panorama interview what her main task was, Fahnbulleh replied: "With the cost of living biting, affordability is my overriding objective, without a doubt."
In the interview, which was recorded last week, and aired on Monday night, she argued that Labour's push for greener electricity was "one of our routes to delivering affordability".
"The drive to clean power is about decoupling our dependence on global fossil fuel markets," she added. "Ultimately if we have homegrown renewables, nuclear, that's the way in which we will drive bills in the long term."
However, she conceded that struggles over energy affordability were part of the reason the consensus on climate action was "under pressure".
"People want to blame net zero for that. Now, I don't believe that's the case.
"But I'm very clear that part of the way in which we build and maintain public consent is that we've got to show that this transition, which we have to do on climate grounds, is good for people's pockets."
Fire and Floods: Our Extreme Weather
The BBC's climate editor, Justin Rowlatt, investigates the impact of the changing climate on our weather.
Watch on BBC iPlayer or on BBC One (BBC Two in Northern Ireland) at 20:00 on Monday 9 November.
The UK had a record number of heatwaves this summer and suffered successive damaging wildfires,which the Met Office has said was made 130 times more likely by climate change.
Just last month, whilst hosting the UK's first summit on wildfires, Andy Burnham acknowledged that as a result of climate change "the summer we've just had is likely to be a more regular situation going forward".
But he has also vowed to lead a "cost of living government" and reindustralise the economy.
This has prompted some in Westminster to speculate that he could demote climate action to help reduce energy costs in the short-term.
His government has dismayed some green activists by diverting funding from the energy department to help meet defence funding targets, including money previously earmarked for energy efficiency schemes.
Last month the governmentapproved drilling at the Jackdaw gas fieldwhich also prompted criticism from some campaigners, although ministers have sought to argue it will minimise imports of higher emission fuels.
A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, located off the coast of Shetland.
Speaking to Panorama, Fahnbulleh insisted reducing carbon emissions "absolutely is a priority", pointing to this summer's droughts as evidence of the need to tackle global warming.
However, she conceded that Labour's target for 95% of electricity generated in Britain to come from clean power sources by 2030 was a "stretch".
On Monday, it was reported that the government is considering weakening the electric vehicle mandate requiring car manufacturers to phase out production of petrol and diesel cars by 2035.
This could prove a blow to not only the country's climate targets but the UK's claim to be providing leadership on the issues just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.
